pages.text: The pale traces at home are the quiet remains of something held in suspension. Elsewhere the same material can carry an ember-lit heartbeat.
pages.title: The Bloom
A fire under bark
pages.text: Living colonies spread from assimilation hearts. Break the heart to stop its colony: attached tissue becomes dormant while preserving its shape. Detached tissue yields dormant flakes rather than finished essence. Cold traces do

pages.title: A fire under bark
pages.text: The approved pale and amber material marks the same organism in both states; a living heartbeat makes the difference.

pages.title: Work from the edge
pages.text: Harvest attached tissue for raw flakes. Recover a heart if you want to build field instruments. Growth lost with its support yields no harvest.

pages.title: Work from the edge
pages.text: Infection requires physical contact with living Bloom tissue or an infected body. Merely standing nearby is safe. Leave contact to let early exposure subside.

pages.title: Work from the edge
pages.text: A Disruption Charm, held in the offhand or worn in a Curios charm slot, blocks new infection. String, amethyst, copper and essence make one. It does not cure an infection already established. Infected creatures keep their bodies

pages.title: Work from the edge
pages.text: but share threats and move as one unsettled mind.

pages.title: Work from the edge
pages.text: This is not proof the Bloom was born here. Only proof it has learned to live here.
